messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] q-value proble
parts:
Please do not double post, you have little power to discriminate differentially methylated regions with 1X coverage, please don't do it!! it is called multiple testing correction, there are many articles and a wiki page about it.
http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multiple_comparisons_problem


On Wed, Dec 3, 2014 at 11:15 PM, raza rahman <raza9p...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hello Everyone,
               I have millions of reads but Just for this question I chosed these two records
> meth   
chr   start     end strand coverage1 numCs1 numTs1 coverage2 numCs2 numTs2
chr1 1234567 1234567      +         1      0      1         2      2      0
chr1 1234568 1234568      +         1      1      0         1      0      1

> myDiff25p = get.methylDiff(myDiff, difference = 25,qvalue = 0.01)
> myDiff25p
 chr   start     end strand    pvalue     qvalue  meth.diff
chr1 1234567 1234567      + 0.3333333 0.00155631 -100.00000
chr1 1234568 1234568      + 1.0000000 0.00155631  100.00000

Can somebody explain to me how methylkit calculate the q-values? I tried fisher_exact test for both the rows manually (by making matrices and using the fisher.test) It shows the p-value is correct for both the cases (0.3333333,1.0000000).

But why is the qvalue same for both the pvalues? It shows me both the rows as significant. Can somebody please explain to me how
are they calculated?

thanks

--
